paper.title: Evolving Medical Imaging Agents via Experience-driven Self-skill Discovery
paper.central_claim: MACRO: mining recurring tool sequences from verified (correct-answer) trajectories into registered composite tools, with image-feature memory and a GRPO stage rewarding composite use, consistently improves multi-step orchestration accuracy and cross-domain generalization of a 3B medical imaging agent over static-toolchain agents.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to the worker; model type per claude-kimi config (haiku slot -> claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]).

evidence.quote: tool sets and invocation strategies are predefined and remain static after deployment
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated gap: medical agents use static tool sets; the object changed is the tool set/action space.

evidence.quote: the agent receives a positive signal when its rollout contains validated composite procedures
evidence.support_explanation: RL reward is tied to composite usage, not to answer correctness.

evidence.quote: is registered as a composite tool when its frequency exceeds a threshold
evidence.support_explanation: Admission rule for composites is a frequency threshold on contiguous tool-name subsequences; threshold value not given in the text.

evidence.quote: This delayed success signal provides a global credit assignment and enables the discovery of new composite patterns, but it does not directly affect the policy gradient updates in Stage 2.
evidence.support_explanation: Final-answer-vs-ground-truth success gates memory/registry writes only; gradient reward is composite-usage.

evidence.quote: This reward encourages the agent to invoke composite tools as a single conceptual unit, thereby promoting more efficient and structured reasoning.
evidence.support_explanation: Reward is intended to increase composite invocation; no term penalises incorrect use of composites.

evidence.quote: Incorporating composite tool discovery without reinforcement yields a substantial leap (REFUGE2 BACC 90.6 %, F1 80.3 %)
evidence.support_explanation: Ablation row C vs B (83.9/75.8): composite registry on/off gives the largest reported jump on REFUGE2; single run, no variance.

evidence.quote: Adding memory store improves recall and F1, particularly on REFUGE2 (F1 +6.1 %).
we achieve gains of 2.3% in BACC and 3.9% in F1 score on glaucoma, and while BACC shows a marginal decrease of 0.6% on heart disease, F1 score improves by a notable 2.6%
evidence.support_explanation: Margin over the strongest agentic baseline (MedAgent-Pro) is small and mixed on MITEA.

evidence.quote: composite quality is fundamentally bounded by trajectory verification fidelity; noisy or partially correct traces risk introducing suboptimal skills into the library.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors concede composite quality control is only trajectory-level and unverified at the composite level.

evidence.quote: The base model is Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct, a 3B parameter vision-language model.
evidence.support_explanation: Only one base model; weight training (LoRA SFT+GRPO) co-occurs with the non-weight registry/memory.

evidence.quote: we first collect high-quality demonstration trajectories from a strong teacher VLM
evidence.support_explanation: A stronger external teacher (DeepSeek) seeds trajectories, memory and the composite registry.

evidence.quote: Extensive experiments across diverse medical imaging datasets and tasks demonstrate that autonomous composite tool discovery consistently improves multi-step orchestration accuracy and cross-domain generalization over strong baselines
evidence.support_explanation: Central claim includes cross-domain generalization; the experiments are per-dataset train/test with no transfer protocol described.

evidence.quote: with some (e.g., ConvKAN) obtaining high specificity (94.70%) but extremely low sensitivity (3.82%)
evidence.support_explanation: Trained task-specific baselines are near chance BACC on imbalanced RAM-W600; baseline strength is questionable.

evidence.quote: To our knowledge, no prior healthcare AI system continuously mines its own clinical experiences to create new composite tool chains.
evidence.support_explanation: Author novelty claim limited to healthcare; general tool-library growth methods (Voyager-type skill libraries, tool makers) are not compared.

evidence.quote: After each training episode, if the final prediction is correct
evidence.support_explanation: Memory writes are gated on ground-truth label agreement during training.

evidence.quote: performance with abstract tools improves by 8.8% over the basic tool lib.
evidence.support_explanation: Within-run comparison of abstract vs basic tool library; correlational with training progress.

gap.author_gap: Medical agents use predefined static tool sets/invocation strategies that are brittle under domain shift and need manual re-design.
gap.checked_gap: Plausible real limitation (fixed toolchain) but the paper presents no measurement of brittleness of static chains beyond comparing to baselines; the genuinely changed non-weight object is the tool/action registry plus memory.
gap.lineage_closest_adjacent: Voyager-style skill libraries, tool-making/ToolMaker agents, MemSkill and EvolveR (cited), Biomni (cited). Only MemSkill, EvolveR and Biomni are cited by the paper; classical skill-library and tool-creation lineages are not compared (source: paper Sec 2, version v1).
gap.residue: Generic skill-library growth already exists; the unaddressed residue is medical-domain composites validated beyond answer match.
gap.stakes: Maintenance cost and degradation when imaging protocols shift; asserted not measured.
gap.method_response: Mine frequent successful tool sequences, register as composites, reward their use.
gap.remaining_gap: Composite admission is by frequency and trajectory success only; no evidence composites are causally useful versus arbitrary usage; no cross-domain/modality shift test.
unresolved: Value of tau and number/identity of discovered composites not in text
Closest non-medical tool-library baselines not run

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In a single-run additive ablation on two public medical datasets, adding memory, mined composite tools and GRPO to a LoRA-tuned 3B agent raises reported BACC/F1; retention to held-out tasks and cross-domain generalization are not shown.

E.causality.reason: Additive ablation isolates memory, composite, GRPO, but no hand-designed/random composite or correctness-aware reward control, and baselines have unequal training exposure.
